indication.text: Supplement adds a feline indication: sedative and analgesic in cats to facilitate clinical examinations, clinical procedures, minor surgical procedures and minor dental procedures.
indication.quote: The effect of the supplement is to add an indication for its use as a sedative and analgesic to facilitate clinical examinations, clinical procedures, minor surgical procedures, and minor dental procedures in cats.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: for sedation and analgesia to facilitate clinical procedures in cats
dose_regimen.quote: The study showed that DEXDOMITOR administered at 40 mcg/kg by the intramuscular (IM) route of administration was effective for sedation and analgesia in cats.

target_animal_safety.duration: 3 consecutive days of daily IM administration

findings.finding: Corneal opacity absent in controls, incidence increased with dose; resolved by 4 h at 1X but persisted at 8 h at 3X and 5X
findings.quote: Corneal opacity resolved by 4 hours in the 1X group but was still present at 8 hours in the 3X and 5X groups.

findings.finding: Miosis seen only in the 5X group
findings.quote: Abnormalities in pupil diameter were not observed in the control group (0X) or in the 1X and 3X groups.

findings.finding: Degree and duration of sedation were dose-related
findings.quote: In the dexmedetomidine treated groups, the degree and duration of sedation were dose-related.

findings.finding: Dose-dependent decrease in heart rate
findings.quote: The mean heart rate showed significantly greater decreases as dose increased (p<0.0001)

findings.finding: Irregular rhythms (junctional escape beats, ventricular complexes) at all dose levels but no AV block
findings.quote: Dexmedetomidine did not induce atrioventricular block under these experimental conditions.

findings.finding: Hypothermia: 7 cats had temperatures below 86 F at hour 8
findings.quote: At hour 8, hypothermic temperatures in 7 cats resulted in missing values that were known to be <86

findings.finding: Injection-site inflammation slightly exacerbated at 3X and 5X
findings.quote: In the intermediate and high dose groups, a slight exacerbation was seen in the severity (minimal to moderate) of the lesion.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Test Animals: Thirty-six (18 male; 18 female), 6 to 8 months of age, healthy, Do mestic Shorthair cats.

effectiveness.design: Masked, randomized, double-dummy, multicenter field study (MPV 03 02) in 242 client-owned cats; 40 mcg/kg IM dexmedetomidine vs active control xylazine 2.2 mg/kg IM; non-inferiority design
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Success rate (score 3 or 4) for ability to perform the procedure 30 minutes after treatment; non-inferiority margin -13%
effectiveness.result: Success rate 91.7% dexmedetomidine vs 87.5% xylazine; lower CI bound of difference (-4%) exceeded the -13% margin, so dexmedetomidine was non-inferior; sedation and pedal-reflex analgesia scores consistently higher than xylazine
effectiveness.quote: Cats in the dexmedetomidine group (n = 122) received an intramuscular injection of dexmedetomidine and an intramuscular injection of a placebo. Cats in the xylazine group (n = 120) received an intramuscular injection of xylazine and an intramuscular injection of a placebo.

notes: Feline supplemental approval; summary states the canine product is unchanged. Adverse reaction rows are from field-study Table 5, columns in order: DEX n, DEX %, XYL n, XYL % (DEX N=122, XYL N=120). TAS design quote says thirty-six cats but the dosing table lists 24 cats (3 male + 3 female per group x 4 groups); a separate 10X (400 mcg/kg) single-dose acute tolerance study in 6 cats is also summarized (all sedated, vomiting in 5 of 6, corneal opacity, hypothermia, no mortality). Some words in the PDF text are split by spaces (e.g. 'Do mestic'); quotes reproduce the extracted text.

indication.text: Supplement adds use as a preanesthetic to general anesthesia in cats.
indication.quote: This supplement provides for a new indication for use as a preanesthetic to general anesthesia in cats.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: given as a preanesthetic prior to induction of general anesthesia (ketamine 5 mg/kg IM or propofol IV in the field study)
dose_regimen.quote: The study showed that DEXDOMITOR administered at 40 mcg/kg by the intramuscular (IM) route was effective as a preanesthetic for cats.

effectiveness.design: Masked, randomized, saline-controlled multicenter field study (#1987C-60-07-319) in 184 client-owned cats; 40 mcg/kg IM dexmedetomidine or saline followed by ketamine 5 mg/kg IM or propofol IV induction; short and long procedures analyzed separately
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Successful intubation after ketamine 5 mg/kg (ketamine arms); amount of propofol needed to attempt intubation (propofol arms)
effectiveness.result: Intubation success with ketamine 88.2% (short) and 90.8% (long) after dexmedetomidine vs 15.8% and 5.5% after saline (P=0.0110, P=0.0201); mean propofol dose 5.65/5.16 mg/kg vs 10.80/10.56 mg/kg (47.7%/51.1% less); isoflurane requirement reduced 35% (ketamine) and 44.4% (propofol); lower post-operative pain VAS
effectiveness.quote: Test animals: One hundred eighty four client-owned cats were enrolled with 116 receiving dexmedetomidine and 68 receiving saline.

adverse_reactions.quote: Decreased body temperature n/a 4 n/a n/a

notes: Feline preanesthetic supplement. No target animal safety studies were required ('CVM did not require target animal safety studies for this supplemental approval'); TAS for cats is in the 2006 and 2007 summaries. Adverse reaction rows are from Table 11 with four columns in order: Saline/ketamine (T01, n=37), Dexmedetomidine/ketamine (T02, n=64), Saline/propofol (T03, n=31), Dexmedetomidine/propofol (T04, n=52); counts are numbers of cats. A dosage characterization study in 36 cats (40 mcg/kg IM then ketamine 5 mg/kg) reported one serious adverse reaction (severe bradycardia, apnea, cardiovascular depression) reversed with atipamezole.

indication.quote: For use as a sedative and analgesic in dogs and cats to facilitate clinical examinations, clinical procedures, minor surgical procedures, and minor dental procedures.

dose_regimen.quote: Dogs: for sedative and analgesic administer 375 mcg/m2 by intravenous (IV) injection or 500 mcg/m2 by intramuscular (IM) injection; for preanesthesia administer 125 or 375 mcg/m2 by IM injection. Cats: for sedation, analgesia, or preanesthesia administer 40 mcg/kg IM.

indication.text: Preanesthetic agent to reduce the amount of barbiturate required for short-duration anesthesia in dogs.
indication.quote: As a preanesthetic agent to reduce the amount barbiturate required for short duration anesthesia in dogs.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: 3-5 minutes before inducing anesthesia with a short-acting barbiturate
dose_regimen.quote: A single intravenous dose of 0.2 mg diazepam/kg body weight, 3-5 minutes before inducing anesthesia with a short acting barbiturate.

target_animal_safety.duration: 30 days daily IV (25X study); other studies 1 dose to 4 weeks
target_animal_safety.n_animals: Four dogs (2 male, 2 female) per group

findings.finding: Moderate to marked increase in alkaline phosphatase at 5 mg/kg/day x30 days
findings.quote: A moderate to marked increase of alkaline phosphatase. Dogs in control group levels were 111 and group 2 had increased levels up to 416 U/L.

findings.finding: Increased liver weight (~15% relative) in treated groups
findings.quote: Increased liver weights were observed in the treated groups. On an absolute basis the mean liver weight of the control dogs was 325 gms vs 434 for the medicated dogs.

findings.finding: Intracanalicular cholestasis more frequent in treated groups
findings.quote: Intracanalicular cholestatsis was observed more often in the treated groups.

findings.finding: Ataxia and sedation for ~3 h after each 5 mg/kg injection, mainly in week 1
findings.quote: Ataxic gait and sedation were observed for approximately three hours after injection, mainly during the first experimental week.

findings.finding: 30-day dosing at 25X confirmed safety of the 0.2 mg/kg dose
findings.quote: This 30-day dosing at 25 times the approved level confirms the safety of the preanesthetic dose of 0.2 mg a.i./kg b.w. of injectable diazepam in the dog (a.i. means active ingredient).

findings.finding: Acute: 5 and 10 mg/kg produced ataxia/sedation; 20 mg/kg produced hypnosis 30-60 min; all survived
findings.quote: Diazepam at 5 and 10 mg/kg I.V. produced ataxia and sedation, while 20 mg/kg I.V. produced hypnosis for 30-60 minutes. All dogs survived and were considered normal by 48 hours postdosing.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Four dogs (2 male, 2 female) were assigned to each treatment group and were injected intravenously with 1 mL Veteeze (5 mg diazepam)/kg daily for a period of 30 days.

effectiveness.design: Blinded, placebo-controlled pivotal clinical study C-88-23 in 90 client dogs (30 per group) randomized to 0.1 or 0.2 mg/kg IV diazepam or sterile water placebo 3-5 min before thiamylal induction; three further field studies (C-89-10, C-89-13, C-89-14) and a 4x4 Latin-square laboratory dose titration in 24 dogs
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Amount of thiamylal (mg/kg) required for satisfactory endotracheal intubation
effectiveness.result: C-88-23: 7.77 mg/kg thiamylal at 0.2 mg/kg diazepam (28% reduction vs control 10.81 mg/kg); 8.8 mg/kg at 0.1 mg/kg (18.6%); pooled four studies: average 20% reduction in thiamylal (P < .017); 0.2 mg/kg consistently superior to 0.1 mg/kg
effectiveness.quote: Ninety (90) dogs of various breeds, age and sex, which were surgical candidates from routine hospital admissions, were randomly assigned by a computer-generated schedule to treatments of 0.1, 0.2 mg/kg body weight of diazepam (as Veteeze Injection) or sterile water placebo.

adverse_reactions.term: Post-operative reactions (hyperexcitability, nausea, vomiting/retching, excessive salivation) in study C-89-10
adverse_reactions.treated: three in each diazepam treatment group
adverse_reactions.quote: Adverse reactions were recorded for 7 dogs; three in each of the treatment groups and one in the placebo group.

notes: 1992 original approval. No pharmacokinetic data in the summary. Adverse reactions were reported only in study C-89-10 (90 dogs); the other three field studies and the titration study reported none. The 25X 30-day study also compared heat-stressed and degradation-product-spiked diazepam; findings were the same in all three treated groups.

species_class: Dogs, puppies, cats and kittens (supplement adds kittens not less than three months of age and adult dogs)

indication.text: Removal and control of roundworms (Toxocara canis, Toxocara cati, Toxascaris leonina) and hookworms (Ancylostoma caninum, Ancylostoma tubaeforme, Uncinaria stenocephala) in dogs, puppies, cats and kittens.
indication.quote: TASK Tabs (dichlorvos) is an anthelmintic product recommended for the removal and control of the roundworms (Toxocara canis, Toxocara cati, Toxascaris leonina) and hookworms (Ancylostoma caninum, Ancylostoma tubaeforme, Uncinaria stenocephala) occurring in the intestinal tract of dogs, puppies, cats and kittens.

dose_regimen.dose: 5 mg dichlorvos per pound body weight
dose_regimen.quote: TASK® Tabs are administered as a single dose to provide 5 mg dichlorvos per pound body weight to dogs, puppies, cats and kittens.

findings.finding: No adverse reactions in adult and geriatric dogs at up to 5X
findings.quote: There were no adverse reactions in noted in this study.

findings.finding: Effectiveness and safety demonstrated in adult and geriatric dogs at doses up to 5X
findings.quote: The study demonstrated the effectiveness and safety of Task Tabs in adult and geriatric dogs when administered at doses up to 5X.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: This study included 15 dogs over 60 pounds. Five geriatric dogs (over 7 years of age) were included in the study. Ten adult dogs (between 1 and 7 years of age) were included in the study.

effectiveness.design: Multi-investigator (14 sites) clinical field study of 5 mg/lb single oral dose in adult dogs; eggs-per-gram reduction and parasite clearance rates; plus a critical (necropsy) test in 25 young adult Beagles and a 12-site field study in 43 kittens 3-5 months old
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Parasite clearance rate (egg counts to zero) and EPG reduction rate
effectiveness.result: Dogs: roundworms cleared 157/171 (91.2%), EPG 549 to 17 (96.9%); hookworms cleared 114/124 (91.9%), EPG 348 to 16 (95.4%). Critical test: T. canis 141/141 (100%), T. leonina 213/292 (73%), A. caninum 147/151 (97.4%) expelled. Kittens: 91% clearance for both roundworms and hookworms
effectiveness.quote: In this study, 171 dogs were treated for roundworm infections and 124 dogs were treated for hookworm infections.

adverse_reactions.term: Cholinergic signs (vomiting, excessive salivation, pupillary contraction, dyspnea, watery diarrhea, muscle fasciculations, abdominal pain, ataxia, general weakness)
adverse_reactions.quote: The most common adverse reactions recorded were vomiting, excessive salivation, pupillary contraction, dyspnea, watery diarrhea, muscle fasciculations, abdominal pain, ataxia, and general weakness.

notes: Supplemental approval (1999) extending use to kittens >= 3 months and adult dogs and adding 10 and 20 mg tablet sizes; data from the 1973 original approval were re-evaluated. No pharmacokinetic content (the batch plan's PK-sentence count reflects 'clearance rate' wording). Adverse reaction counts are not given in the summary. The TAS entry is Clinical Study 1 (dose-multiple study in 15 large dogs); doses are described as approximating 1X, 2X and 5X.

indication.text: Prevention of heartworm (Dirofilaria immitis) and hookworm (Ancylostoma caninum) infection, removal and control of whipworms (Trichuris vulpis) and, per this supplement, removal and control of mature and immature intestinal Toxocara canis (ascarids) in dogs.
indication.quote: FILARIBITS Plus are indicated for use in the prevention of infection with Dirofilaria immitis (heartworm disease), Ancylostoma caninum (hookworm infection), the removal and control of Trichuris vulpis (whipworm infection) and the removal and control of mature and immature stages of intestinal Toxocara canis (ascarid infection) in dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: 3 mg diethylcarbamazine citrate and 2.27 mg oxibendazole per pound of body weight
dose_regimen.route: oral (chewable tablet, free-choice or on food)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: continuous daily administration throughout the period of hookworm/mosquito exposure
dose_regimen.quote: FILARIBITS Plus are given orally (once a day) at a dosage rate of 3 mg diethylcarbamazine citrate and 2.27 mg oxibendazole per pound of body weight.

findings.finding: Side effects (vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, tenesmus, depression, elevated ALP and WBC) in 4 field-trial dogs
findings.quote: Investigators in the clinical trials reported one or more of the following side effects in a total of 4 dogs: vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, tenesmus and depression plus elevated serum alkaline phosphatase and white blood cell count levels.

findings.finding: Boxed warning for occasional hepatic toxicity including fatalities
findings.quote: Labeling contains a boxed warning that addresses the occasional association with hepatic toxicity including several fatalities.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: No adverse reactions or unusual observations associated with FILARIBITS Plus were reported by investigators conducting the critical laboratory trials. Untoward reactions in the clinical trials were minimal in number as well as severity.

effectiveness.design: Clinical field trials at 18 practices in 12 states in ascarid-infected dogs given FILARIBITS Plus daily (average 73.5 days); 7 pivotal investigators also ran FILARIBITS (diethylcarbamazine only) controls (11 dogs); plus four critical laboratory studies (each dog its own control) in 42 dogs
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent of dogs cleared of ascarids at fecal rechecks (approx. 30, 60 and 90 days)
effectiveness.result: Field: significantly more dogs cleared with FILARIBITS Plus than FILARIBITS (Mantel-Haenszel P<0.02); pivotal T1 group 100% (31/31) cleared at rechecks 1 and 2 vs 72.7% (8/11) and 70% (7/10) for FILARIBITS controls. Laboratory: 100% ascarid removal in all four critical studies after 30 days
effectiveness.quote: In the clinical (field) trials, 68 dogs from eighteen veterinary practices in twelve states were studied. All dogs were infected with ascarids when entering the study.

adverse_reactions.term: Vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, tenesmus, depression, elevated ALP and WBC (one or more)
adverse_reactions.quote: Investigators in the clinical trials reported one or more of the following side effects in a total of 4 dogs: vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, tenesmus and depression plus elevated serum alkaline phosphatase and white blood cell count levels.

notes: 1989 Category II supplemental approval adding the ascarid claim; no new target animal safety studies (safety data unchanged, refers to original FOI summary), no PK. Target_animal_safety here records field-trial safety observations only, with no dose-multiple study. Tables VI/VII give per-investigator clearance data.

indication.text: Management of diseases in dogs associated with bacteria susceptible to difloxacin; clinical efficacy confirmed in skin and soft tissue infections (wounds, abscesses) and urinary tract infections (cystitis).
indication.quote: DICURAL® (difloxacin hydrochloride) TABLETS are indicated for the management of diseases in dogs associated with bacteria susceptible to difloxacin.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: 2-3 days beyond cessation of clinical signs to a maximum of 30 days; urinary tract infections at least 10 consecutive days
dose_regimen.quote: The dose range of difloxacin in dogs is 5 to 10 mg/kg (2.3 to 4.6 mg/lb) once a day for 2-3 days beyond cessation of clinical signs to a maximum of 30 days.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: AUCinfinity, single oral 5 mg/kg, fasted, two-period crossover, 2 groups of 10 dogs; columns Tablet, Capsule
pharmacokinetics.quote: AUCinfinity mcg·hr/mL 14.5 16.2

pharmacokinetics.conditions: elimination T1/2, single oral 5 mg/kg, fasted; columns Tablet, Capsule
pharmacokinetics.quote: Elimination Half-Life (T1/2) hr 9.3 9.4

pharmacokinetics.conditions: single oral 5 mg/kg, fasted; columns Tablet, Capsule
pharmacokinetics.quote: Maximum Concentration (Cmax) mcg/mL 1.8 2.1

pharmacokinetics.conditions: single oral 5 mg/kg, fasted; columns Tablet, Capsule
pharmacokinetics.quote: Maximum Time (Tmax) hr 2.8 2.3

pharmacokinetics.conditions: 14C-difloxacin base 10 mg/kg oral gavage, fasted, 6 beagles
pharmacokinetics.quote: After oral administration of a 10 mg base/kg dose, both the total radioactivity and parent drug levels in the plasma peaked at 2.4 mcg/mL by 1.5 hours.

pharmacokinetics.value: 16% of dose in urine, 80% in feces within five days
pharmacokinetics.conditions: excretion of 14C after oral 10 mg/kg
pharmacokinetics.quote: Within five days after oral administration of 14C-difloxacin base, 16% of the 14C dose was excreted in the urine and 80% was eliminated in the feces.

pharmacokinetics.value: renal clearance <5% of total systemic clearance
pharmacokinetics.conditions: after IV 14C-difloxacin; biliary secretion and enterohepatic cycling important
pharmacokinetics.quote: Renal clearance accounted for less than 5% of the total systemic clearance.

pharmacokinetics.value: 1.39 +/- 0.44 µg/mL (mean plasma concentration three hours post-dose, 5 mg/kg/day)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 3-month oral dosing, mean of hour-3 samples on days 0, 6, 28, 56 and 84; columns dose, observed mean +/- SD, dose-normalized, %CV; no accumulation with repeated dosing

dose_multiples: 5X (25 mg/kg/day; 2.5X the 10 mg/kg upper label dose)

findings.finding: Diarrhea and transient erythema/edema of ears, face, lips and periocular skin
findings.quote: Antemortem observations included diarrhea and transient erythema/edema. Erythema and edema (red/warm) were observed on the ears, face, lips, and around the eyes.

findings.finding: No radiocarpal joint flattening in skeletally mature dogs
findings.quote: There were no confirmed occurrences of flattening (hyperextension) of the radiocarpal joint.

findings.finding: No quinolone-type articular cartilage lesions in mature dogs
findings.quote: There were no articular cartilage lesions characteristic of quinolone-induced arthropathy of juvenile dogs.

findings.finding: 10-day 50 mg/kg/day study: difloxacin glucuronide particles in gall bladder bile of 3 of 4 dogs, with orange emesis/feces
findings.quote: Gross necropsy revealed granular-like particles of the glucuronide ester of difloxacin in the bile within the gall bladder in three of the four dogs administered 50 mg/kg/day BW for 10 days.

findings.finding: 13-week juvenile study: dose-related radiocarpal joint hyperextension above 5 mg/kg
findings.quote: An increased incidence of bilateral flattening (hyperextension) of the radiocarpal joint was noted at dose levels greater than 5 mg/kg and was dose related.

findings.finding: 13-week juvenile study: articular cartilage lesions mainly at 50 and 125 mg/kg
findings.quote: Drug-related effects were found in the articular cartilage of the femur and proximal tibia, principally in the animals given 50 or 125 mg/kg.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Dogs were dosed at levels of at 5, 15 or 25 mg/kg of body weight/day (mg/kg) for 30 days. A control group (four/sex) received placebo tablets for 30 days.

effectiveness.design: Multi-center (18 veterinarians, 4 US regions) randomized clinical field trial of difloxacin tablets 5.0 mg/kg once daily vs enrofloxacin 2.5 mg/kg twice daily (positive control) for 5-10 days in dogs with dermal and urinary tract infections
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Bacterial elimination (urinary tract) and resolution of clinical signs (dermal) at day 5 and 3-5 days post-treatment
effectiveness.result: Difloxacin: urinary E. coli 20/20 (100%), Proteus 5/5 (100%), Staph 6/7 (86%); dermal Staph 36/38 (95%), E. coli 1/1, Klebsiella 1/2 (50%). Enrofloxacin: urinary E. coli 9/10 (90%), dermal Staph 32/34 (94%). Laboratory dose titration selected 5.0 mg/kg; tablet shown bioequivalent to capsule
effectiveness.quote: Difloxacin was administered to 141 dogs of various breeds, weights and ages. The variety of breeds depicted the U.S. canine population. Body weights and ages ranged from 1.4 to 55.9 kg and 9 months to 16 years, respectively. No breed, weight or age susceptibilities were observed. Enrofloxacin was used in a group of 131 dogs, as a positive control for comparative purposes.

adverse_reactions.quote: Nineteen of 131 (14.5%) enrofloxacin-treated dogs and 17 of 141 (12.1%) difloxacin-treated dogs were noted by the investigators to have experienced side effects such as: emesis, anorexia, diarrhea and inappetance.

notes: 1997 original approval. Bioequivalence table (Table 1) rows are quoted as extracted, values in order Tablet then Capsule. Table 3 steady-state row columns: dose (mg/kg), observed hour-3 mean +/- SD, dose-normalized mean, %CV. TAS entry is the 30-day margin-of-safety study in skeletally mature beagles; the 10-day 50 mg/kg tolerance study and 13-week juvenile (3.5-3.8 month) toxicity study (0-125 mg/kg) are captured as additional findings. Field-trial Table 4 was flattened; results were read from the row values.

indication.quote: Indications: For the management of obesity in dogs

dose_regimen.dose: 0.01 mL/kg once daily for 14 days, then 0.02 mL/kg for the next 14 days
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: 5 mg/mL oral solution; after day 28 dose adjusted monthly (increase 100% then 50%) to maintain >= 0.7% weight loss per week; 3-month weight-management phase with 50% then 25% adjustments; maximum 0.2 mL/kg/day
dose_regimen.quote: This characterization supports an initial dose of 0.01 mL/kg of dirlotapide oral solution administered once daily by mouth for 14 days followed by 0.02 mL/kg for the next 14 days.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: oral 2.5-10 mg/kg once daily for 14 days, beagles; increased with dose and repeated dosing
pharmacokinetics.quote: The mean elimination half-life ranged between 5 and 18 hours, and it seemed to increase with dose and with repeated administration.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: Day 1, 0.5 mg/kg oral, obese beagles (3-month margin-of-safety study)
pharmacokinetics.quote: Cmax on Day 1 at the 0.5 mg/kg dose was 63.5 (+ 27.7 SD) ng/mL and AUC0-last was 304 (+ 134) ng*h/mL.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: Day 1, 0.5 mg/kg oral, obese beagles
pharmacokinetics.quote: Cmax on Day 1 at the 0.5 mg/kg dose was 63.5 (+ 27.7 SD) ng/mL and AUC0-last was 304 (+ 134) ng*h/mL.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: dirlotapide and one metabolite detected in bile in a greater-than-dose-proportional manner
pharmacokinetics.quote: Dirlotapide clearance appears to be primarily via biliary secretion.

pharmacokinetics.value: systemic exposure highest on Day 29, then decreased during the subsequent two months
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 0.5-2.5 mg/kg/day oral, 3 months
pharmacokinetics.quote: Systemic exposure was highest on Day 29, and decreased during the subsequent two months of treatment.

target_animal_safety.duration: 90 consecutive days once daily, plus 1-month post-treatment period for selected dogs

findings.finding: Dose-related vomiting in the first 14 days: 5/6 (2.5 mg/kg), 9/12 (1.5 mg/kg), 2/6 (0.5 mg/kg)
findings.quote: During the first 14 days of treatment, 5 of 6 dogs (87%) in the 2.5 mg/kg group, 9 of 12 (75%) in the 1.5 mg/kg group, and 2 of 6 (33%) in the 0.5 mg/kg treatment group vomited.

findings.finding: Body weight fell 17-39% from baseline in treated dogs
findings.quote: Body weight decreased between 17% and 39% from baseline for dirlotapide-treated dogs.

findings.finding: Mild to moderate ALT/AST increases at 1.5 and 2.5 mg/kg; two high-dose dogs had AST >100 U/L with ALT >500 U/L
findings.quote: In the high dose (2.5 mg/kg) group, two of six dogs (one male and one female) had AST elevations >100 U/L combined with ALT elevations >500 U/L and a mild increase in bile acids.

findings.finding: Dose-related decreases in serum cholesterol and HDL
findings.quote: Dogs treated wi th dirlotapide revealed a dose-related decrease in serum cholesterol (P=0.0001) and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentration (P=0.0001) by day 28 that remained relatively constant for the remainder of the 3-month treatment period.

findings.finding: Reduced plasma vitamins A and E without clinical deficiency
findings.quote: Decreases in vitamin A and E plasma concentrations were observed early in treatment for all dirlotapide-treated groups. No clinical or histopathological signs of vitamin deficiency were observed.

findings.finding: Lipid vacuoles in small-intestinal enterocytes; hepatic glycogen accumulation; reversible after 1-month recovery
findings.quote: On histopathological examination, the enterocytes of the small intestine contained lipid vacuoles in the villus tips. Dilated lacteals were observed in some dogs. Hepatic glycogen accumulation was observed in all treatment groups. There were no significant treatment-related findings at the end of the 1-month recovery period.

findings.finding: Well tolerated at 0.4 mg/kg for 3 months; higher doses increased vomiting and salivation
findings.quote: Dirlotapide was well-tolerated when administered once daily for three months at 0.4 mg/kg to healthy beagle dogs.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: The 38 animals were allocated into 4 groups of dogs. Selected dogs from the 1.5 mg/kg treatment group and 0.3 mL/kg control group were maintained for a 1-month post-treatment period following 3 months of dirlotapide treatment.

effectiveness.design: Randomized, masked, corn-oil-controlled field dose-confirmation study (1962C-60-03-671) at 23 clinics in the US and Canada; 1 control : 2 dirlotapide allocation; escalating 0.0045 then 0.009 mL/lb once daily for 28 days then monthly adjustment for 4 months
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Total percent body weight loss at day 112 and percent of dogs achieving 13% body weight loss at day 112
effectiveness.result: Least squares mean weight change -11.8% dirlotapide vs -3.9% control (P<0.0001); 39% of treated dogs vs 5.3% of controls lost >13% body weight (P=0.0002); 58% of owners reported increased activity; final mean dose 0.12 mg/lb (0.05-0.24)
effectiveness.quote: The study included 258 client owned obese dogs (119 males and 139 fem ales) of various breeds and age (range of 1 to 14 years) presented to 23 veterinary clinics in the US and Canada for weight loss.

notes: 2006 original approval. Adverse reaction rows are from field-study Table 3 (Control n = 88, Dirlotapide n = 170); columns in order Control %, Dirlotapide %. Effectiveness analyses used n = 74/132 (percent weight change) and 75/141 (13% loss endpoint) after withdrawals. PK values come from the target-animal-safety studies (no dedicated PK section). The pivotal margin-of-safety study is the 3-month 0/0.5/1.5/2.5 mg/kg study in obese beagles (Table 9 lists 10 + 4 controls, 6, 12 and 6 dogs). A 14-day 2.5-10 mg/kg tolerance study, a 1-year use-dose study in 72 Labradors (retinal/cataract findings judged breed-related) and a 9-month SEDDS-formulation study are also summarized. Treated dogs in the field study had more ALT (9.9% vs 4.8%) and AST (9.2% vs 6.0%) elevations than controls; one treated Beagle developed seizures and one treated Dachshund a hepatopathy. Some words in the extracted text are split (e.g. 'fem ales', 'wi th'); quotes reproduce the extraction.

indication.text: Dogs, cats and horses: to stimulate respiration during and after general anesthesia and to speed awakening and return of reflexes after anesthesia; neonate dogs and cats: to initiate/stimulate respiration following cesarean section or dystocia.
indication.quote: For dogs, cats and horses: To stimulate respirations during and after general anesthesia. To speed awakening and return of reflexes after anesthesia. For neonate dogs and cats: Initiate respirations following cesarean section or dystocia.

dose_regimen.route: intravenous (adults); subcutaneous, sublingual or umbilical vein (neonates)

effectiveness.design: Waiver from in vivo bioequivalence study (generic of DOPRAM-V, NADA 034-879); no new safety or effectiveness data
effectiveness.result: Biowaiver granted based on formulation characteristics (sterile solution, same active ingredient, concentration and dosage form as the pioneer)
effectiveness.quote: Based on the formulation characteristics of the generic product, Modern Veterinary Therapeutics, LLC was granted a waiver from the requirement of an in vivo bioequivalence study for the generic product RESPIRAM (doxapram hydrochloride solution).

product_name: Doxirobe™ Gel (summary: HESKA Periodontal Disease Therapeutic)

indication.text: Treatment and control of periodontal disease in dogs.
indication.quote: HESKA Periodontal Disease Therapeutic is indicated for the treatment and control of periodontal disease in dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: 8.5% doxycycline (as doxycycline hyclate) flowable gel; as many units as required to fill the periodontal pockets
dose_regimen.route: subgingival (topical) application into periodontal pockets of affected teeth
dose_regimen.frequency: single administration (product forms a slow-release polymer depot)
dose_regimen.quote: Once mixed, the product is a flowable solution of doxycycline hyclate equivalent to 8.5% doxycycline activity. The formulation is applied subgingivally to the periodontal pocket(s) of affected teeth, and doxycycline is slowly released from the polymer providing a local antimicrobial effect. Use as many units as required to fill the periodontal pockets of affected teeth.

pharmacokinetics.value: plasma doxycycline detectable only at 6 and 12 hours (dogs with four treated sites)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: subgingival 5% and 10% doxycycline hyclate formulations, 6 beagles (ATS-32); total doses 13.7-22.6 mg in the dogs with detectable levels
pharmacokinetics.quote: Detectable plasma doxycycline concentrations were present in the three dogs which had four treated sites, but only at 6 and 12 hours after treatment onset (Table 5).

pharmacokinetics.value: no plasma drug after 12 hours post-treatment
pharmacokinetics.conditions: sampling at 6, 12, 24 h, daily to day 6, then days 10-28
pharmacokinetics.quote: No drug was detected in any plasma sample after 12 hours post-treatment

pharmacokinetics.value: gingival crevicular fluid doxycycline exceeded MIC of most periodontal pathogens
pharmacokinetics.conditions: ATS-65 dose confirmation study
pharmacokinetics.quote: Gingival crevicular fluid concentrations of doxycycline exceeded the minimum inhibitory concentration of most periodontal pathogens.

dose_multiples: 5% and 10% doxycycline hyclate formulations (label formulation is 10% hyclate = 8.5% doxycycline)

findings.finding: No tissue irritation attributable to the product (GLP study ATS-31)
findings.quote: This study demonstrated the lack of tissue irritation when the test articles were placed into naturally occurring periodontal pockets in the dog.

findings.finding: Gingivitis incidence comparable between 5%, 10% and saline control sites
findings.quote: The microscopic and macroscopic incidence of gingivitis was comparable between the 5% and 10% formulations and the control sites.

findings.finding: ATS-32: mild erythema/edema for ~3 days in treated and control sites, attributed to scaling
findings.quote: Mild inflammation characterized by erythema and edema was present for approximately three days after treatment in treated and control sites and was attributed to the dental scaling procedure.

findings.finding: Only one emesis observation, attributed to anesthetic recovery
findings.quote: Emesis was noted in the cage of one dog (treated with 5% doxycycline) at 2 and 4 hours after treatment administration. The finding was attributed to anesthetic recovery.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Animals: Twelve adult (6.5-10 years), 7.5-16.5 kg, female Beagle dogs with naturally occurring periodontal disease.

effectiveness.design: Dose confirmation study ATS-53 in adult female Beagles with naturally occurring periodontal disease, each dog's baseline as control, 3 teeth/dog, evaluated for 9 months after a single subgingival application; supported by ATS-65 (5 dogs, 4 months) and a vehicle-control study ATS-58 (4 dogs)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Periodontal pocket depth, attachment level and bleeding on probing over time
effectiveness.result: Significant (p<0.001) reductions: mean pocket depth 6.10 mm at baseline to 3.43-3.93 mm, attachment level 4.93 to 2.40 mm and bleeding on probing 2.43 to 0.73 at 9 months; total bacterial counts reduced within two weeks and maintained 9 months; vehicle alone did not change pocket depth or attachment level
effectiveness.quote: Animals: Four adult (7-10 years) female Beagle dogs with naturally occurring periodontal disease.

adverse_reactions.term: None attributed to treatment (ATS-53 treatment sites)
adverse_reactions.quote: No adverse reactions attributed to the treatment were observed at the treatment sites.

notes: 1997 original approval (Heska Corporation; product later marketed as Doxirobe Gel). No dose-multiple margin-of-safety study: safety was assessed by local tissue-irritation studies with 5% and 10% formulations (ATS-32, six dogs, 28 days; ATS-31, twelve dogs, 7-28 days). Effectiveness studies are small laboratory studies (4-5 dogs) with no field trial. PK content is limited to plasma detectability and gingival crevicular fluid statements.

findings.finding: 7-10 month cats: no clinically significant changes at up to 25 mg/kg/day for 30 days
findings.quote: There were no clinically significant changes or biologically significant trends with regard to any of the monitored parameters, i.e., clinical signs, body weights, clinical chemistries/hematology and gross necropsy.

findings.finding: Occasional vomiting in treated and control young cats
findings.quote: Occasional vomition was experienced by 2 of 4 animals receiving 5 mg/kg (IX), 3 of 4 receiving 15 mg/kg (3X), 2 of 4 receiving 25 mg/kg (SX)and 1 of 4 nontreated controls.

findings.quote: Clinical signs of toxicosis induced in the 4 treated cats were salivation, change in behavior, vomition, inappetance, depression, muscle tremors, incoordination and convulsions.

findings.finding: Both cats at 125 mg/kg/day (25X) died on days 4 and 5
findings.quote: The 2 cats receiving the daily treatments of 125 mg/kg expired on days 4 and 5.

findings.finding: 5-7 month kittens: articular cartilage lesions in the 2 males given 25 mg/kg/day for 30 days
findings.quote: Findings at necropsy indicated no significant lesions of the soft tissues, however, the 2 male cats that received 25 mg/kg daily treatments had lesions of the articular cartilage.

findings.finding: 3-4 month kittens: no articular cartilage lesions at up to 25 mg/kg/day for 30 days

target_animal_safety.design_quote: The enrofloxacin 5.7 mg tablets were administered orally twice daily to the 3 groups (4 animals each) at 2.5, 7.5 and 12.5 mg/kg or at a total daily dose of 5, 15 and 25 mg/kg (2.27, 6.8 and 11.34 mg/lb) for 30 consecutive days.

effectiveness.design: Well-controlled, blinded multi-site (22 practitioners) clinical trial in cats with naturally occurring bacterial infections, enrofloxacin tablets 2.5 mg/kg BID for up to 10 days vs Hetacin K (hetacillin) 50 mg BID positive control; efficacy by clinical score reduction, pathogen elimination and subjective ratings
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction in clinical score by body system and pathogen elimination on post-treatment culture
effectiveness.result: Dermal clinical score reduction 91.5% (65 cases) enrofloxacin vs 88.5% (72) Hetacin K; dermal pathogen elimination 98.6% (71 isolates) vs 93.8% (81); overall pathogen elimination 91.3% vs 88.7%; efficacy rated excellent/good in 93.7% vs 91.1%; no drug-related side effects
effectiveness.quote: Clinical evaluations were subsequently conducted on 223 cats, 111 dosed with enrofloxacin and 112 with the positive control {Table 2}.

adverse_reactions.quote: No drug-related side effects were observed during this study with either antibacterial.

adverse_reactions.term: Safety rated excellent by practitioners (field safety confirmation, 124 cats)

notes: 1990 supplemental approval adding cats to a dog NADA; the summary is a feline summary (dog data are cross-referenced to the 1989 original). PK values are from the dog-vs-cat serum bioequivalence study (Table 1, columns Dogs then Cats; 24 dogs, 22 cats) and the feline tissue distribution study (Table 7, columns 2, 6 and 12 hours; tissue levels mcg/g, fluid levels mcg/mL). The TAS design quote is the 30-day study in 7-10 month old cats; additional 30-day studies in 3-4 month and 5-7 month kittens, a 15-day liquid-formulation study in 8-10 week kittens, and a 6-day 50/125 mg/kg tolerance test are captured as findings. OCR artifacts ('}' for ')', 'IX', 'SX', 'P<O.OS') are reproduced verbatim in quotes.
